Nothing here is wrong — the PR does what it claims — but it exists to be a proof, and four of its assertions are weaker than the proof needs at exactly the coordinates PR 2 could break.

THE CONSTRAINT HELD (checked myself, not taken from Nicola). HEAD is the merge base 072153a, so the working tree IS the whole PR. Diff against 072153a for server/supabase/functions/ is empty; collab/index.ts is blob 57189c6ce4cee6b2c3de85d14d5ebb9b45133bc9 at 20d11e1, at 072153a and in the working tree alike, so the spike's line numbers hold. collab.test.mjs, schema.test.mjs and jsonb-params.test.mjs are untouched. No untracked files. Three files, 983 insertions; 13 new top-level cases (21 -> 34).

COUNTS I SAW MYSELF
- node --test test/server/functions.test.mjs: 118 tests, 117 pass, 1 fail, 0 SKIPPED, 43.3s, against the unmodified function. The one failure is '/otp short-circuits the reviewer address' at :1381 — pre-existing, outside the new block, the documented per-email 429 from repeated runs on one stack; it cannot fire on a runner's fresh DB.
- SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1 npm test: 1758 tests, 0 fail, 122 skipped. The no-stack skip path is green.

FINDINGS
F1 (material) :3248 and :3253 — assert.equal(scenePull.body.bytes, scene.length) and assert.equal(takePull.body.saved_at, savedAt) compare with ==. scene_bytes and saved_at are bigint (0016_collabs.sql:28, :84), which postgres.js returns as STRINGS, which is why index.ts:1170 and :1191 wrap both in Number(). Drop either wrapper in the move and the body carries "512"; '512' == 512 keeps both green. Same shape at :2891, :2896, :2925, :3242. Fix: strictEqual/deepStrictEqual for these numerics. This is the single hole that sits exactly where a non-pure move would show.
F2 :2661, :2760, :2895, :2911, :2912 — five assert.equal(x, null). undefined == null, so a response that drops the key entirely reads as "null, as documented". A key lost from a moved response-builder is PR 2's likeliest slip and these five are the assertions covering it. Fix: strictEqual.
F3 :2656 — assert.ok(still.claims[0].lastSeenAt >= hot.claims[0].lastSeenAt, 'but it does refresh the lease'). Unchanged satisfies >=, so deleting the lease refresh at index.ts:821 leaves it green. A bare > risks a same-millisecond flake, so the fix is to assert the refresh in a way that can actually fail, not just to flip the operator.
F4 :2390-2391 — the budget comment says the cases spend "eleven" joins. They spend twelve (:2483 :2493 :2497 :2509 :2689 :2766 :2824 :2880 :2958 :3012 :3116 :3212), all charged at index.ts:318 ahead of any code validation. 18 of the 30/h left, not 19 — and at twelve, a third local run inside the hour starts 429ing, which is the same class as the /otp failure I hit.
F5 :2490, :2988, :3030 — all three ticketed behaviours are RECORDED, not endorsed (verified by reading the comments), which is what a characterization test owes. But none names its ticket, though the file already cites keys this way at :2280 ("0042, BAD-008"). Add BAD-064, BAD-063, BAD-065 so the later fix is grep-able.
F6 (minor) :2540 asserts report-by-code's status but not its {ok:true}; :2653 and :2964 assert a body but not its status.
Not findings: no assertion contradicts the source; both odd shapes are pinned correctly — join refuses {allowed:false, reason} with no code key (index.ts:432/451/456) and the test asserts !('code' in body) at :2487; fail() is {error, code} equal and the tests pin both. Nothing reads the function's text, globs the directory or imports from inside collab/ — the only import added is the size caps from _shared/ at :14-16 — so nothing passes only before or only after the split. Nothing can skip on a started stack; a missing bucket fails a 200-assertion rather than bailing.

THE CI HALF
- Verified: node --input-type=module -e "...MAX_SCENE_BYTES..." run from server/ prints 524288000 on this machine's node v26.8.2 AND inside node:22-trixie-slim, the .nvmrc version CI uses, so the constant read is not a local-node accident. 524288000 is MAX_SCENE_BYTES (_shared/collab.mjs:79) and matches the README's retyped value.

- Verified by my own request: a duplicate create POST answers HTTP 400 with {"statusCode":"409","error":"Duplicate","code":"BucketAlreadyExists"}. The step's comment is exactly right and its body-matching is the correct discriminator; matching on HTTP status alone would retry 30 times and fail every re-run.
- COULD NOT RUN: the from-scratch 200 path. This session's permission classifier refused deleting the live bucket ("Interfere With Workloads") and refused creating a probe bucket ("Modify Shared Resources"), so I could not delete-and-recreate. What I have is the artifact, not the act: the bucket on this stack carries exactly the step's parameters. The step's success branch fires on 200|201, which is what storage-api answers on create. Flagging this as the one thing in my brief I did not do.
- Step order is right: start -> assert migrations -> create bucket -> serve -> suite, so the bucket exists before anything signs and after the stack is healthy. set -euo pipefail plus the -z guard means an unreadable SERVICE_ROLE_KEY fails the step rather than sending an empty bearer (I hit exactly that by accident with DOCKER_HOST unset: 400 "Invalid Compact JWS").

- BUDGET — NOT a concern, with numbers. The last 11 Server integration runs took 3m51s to 4m36s against timeout-minutes: 20. storage-api is ~879 MB uncompressed against ~3.4 GB for the rest of the non-excluded set (kong 153 + gotrue 58 + postgres 2040 + postgrest 20 + pg-meta 416 + edge-runtime 690 + mailpit 34), so +26% of image bytes. On a 4-minute job with pull at two thirds that is roughly +40s of pull plus a health wait and the new cases' runtime: call it 5 to 5.5 minutes. Fourteen-plus minutes of headroom, and 4.3 GB of images against 14 GB of disk. imgproxy stays excluded and storage-api is healthy without it — confirmed on this stack, where imgproxy is stopped and the signed-URL round trip passes.

## Outcome
Accepted, and it earned the tier. F1 is the finding that justifies the whole review: scene_bytes and saved_at are bigint and come back as strings, which is why the handlers wrap them in Number() — so == would keep a test green after PR 2 dropped a wrapper, exactly the class of silent regression these tests exist to catch. F2 is the same shape (undefined == null hides a dropped key) and is PR 2's likeliest slip. The budget question is settled with real numbers rather than an estimate: 3m51s-4m36s over the last eleven runs, storage-api adding roughly a quarter of the image bytes. She verified the constraint by blob hash rather than by trusting the diff, and was straight about the one check she could not run: the classifier refused deleting or creating a bucket, so the from-scratch create path is proven only by the artifact and the re-run, and the PR's own first CI run is what will prove the create itself.
